vethra_policy: Every companion who passed through the Keeping bears Vethra, including Harrow's dead flesh. The company displays it as costly first light beneath ash and creaturely firstfruits of fuller light in Christ, but the myth uses only a few representative glimpses rather than an individual roster.
vethra_morning_note: D-085 supersedes the earlier four-person narrative selection. Murn and Keld remain bearers, but their separate Vethra portraits are omitted because their relations are already carried by tending and communal action. Vaerun does not certify his own Vethra. Little Vey displays his through embodied presence beside Vaerun. Proposed portrait language remains available for later correspondence or other contexts.

characters.name: Vaerun
characters.source_role: office of crossing; one bound to pass the veil
characters.title_continuity: before the hill he is a Vaerun among other possible bearers of the crossing vocation; after the hill the many call him the Vaerun, creating singular public stature rather than a new office
characters.continuity: survives the Keeping with a serious scar along his side; the wound is not Vethra, a credential, or proof that suffering improved him
characters.vethra_portrait: At a threshold, his weight fell toward the one still behind, as though crossing were a thing borne between them.

characters.name: Harrow
characters.working_theme: refusal to yield / possible authority theme
characters.continuity: sole named companion who dies during the Keeping; mortally wounded in the assault, carried inside the circle, tended, and absent from the living company in earthly morning; his dead flesh bears Vethra without animation, preservation, radiance, or resurrection
characters.vethra_portrait: The Gravane covered him last. Their hands lingered at his brow; the first light was borne even there, though no breath returned.

characters.name: Sable
characters.continuity: survives the Keeping with a weakened voice that sometimes breaks in song and bears Vethra; the wound is not Vethra
characters.vethra_portrait: When his weakened song broke, the silence did not close; it widened enough for another breath.

characters.name: Murn
characters.continuity: survives aged and embodied with damaged ribs and permanently roughened breath; his young face does not return, his humor remains living, he bears Vethra, and the wound is not Vethra
characters.vethra_portrait: His breath remained rough; when he laughed, fear beside him was not shamed into silence.

characters.name: Little Vey
characters.source_role: small / ember / last light under ash
characters.continuity: survives the Keeping as a living embodied companion and bears Vethra; his only lasting wound is one torn ear, received after he hears the sheep's soft answer, which leaves him hearing poorly on that side; the wound is not Vethra
characters.vethra_portrait: He stood near without drawing the eye; only when he moved did others see whom he had kept from standing alone.
characters.epistolary_role: writes to challenge the movement from a Vaerun to the Vaerun and to summon him back to shared remembrance beneath the Shepherd
characters.epistolary_source: source/book-of-the-troth/The Letter of Little Vey to the Vaerun.md

characters.name: Brindle
characters.source_role: broad-backed and gentle; carried a starving cub
characters.continuity: survives the Keeping with a bent and painful back and bears Vethra; the wound is not Vethra
characters.vethra_portrait: His bent back made shelter, but none beneath it seemed possessed.

characters.source_role: hard of jaw, slow to anger, deep silence
characters.continuity: survives the Keeping without a newly specified lasting physical injury and bears Vethra
characters.vethra_portrait: His silence no longer made a wall; within it another voice could finish.

characters.continuity: survives the Keeping without a newly specified lasting physical injury and bears Vethra
characters.vethra_portrait: He trembled at blood as before, but his paws turned toward the one who bled.
